title: AI Agentic Engineer & Orchestration Manager
description: What we do We run a venture studio building multiple operating ventures (web platforms, AI products, internal tools). We're building an ecosystem of AI agents from scratch, Claude, Codex, Cursor, MCP servers, custom pipelines, to design, build, ship, and maintain these ventures. We need someone who can plug into that ecosystem and become an operator inside it. What is a "vibe coder"? It is someone who builds working software by directing AI tools instead of typing every line by hand. You describe what you want, you read what the AI produces, you test it, you push back when it is wrong, you ship it. You do not need a CS degree but developers are a bonus***. You need taste, judgment, and the ability to learn fast. What you will actually do** - Use AI coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, ChatGPT, etc.) to build and ship features across our ventures - Orchestrate AI agents to run repeatable workflows (research, code review, content, deployment) - Read code carefully enough to know when the AI is lying to you - Run tests, fix bugs, deploy to Vercel / similar platforms - Document what you build so the next AI session can pick up where you left off - Work directly with the founder on whatever venture is hot that week **Who we are looking for** - Obsessed with AI tools, you already use ChatGPT or Claude daily for non-trivial work - Can read JavaScript, Python, or TypeScript well enough to debug — you do not need to write it from scratch - Comfortable in a terminal (git, npm, basic bash) - Fast learner, when you hit something new, you figure it out in hours, not weeks - Written English strong enough to write clear prompts and clear documentation - Honest about what you do not know **Bonus (not required)** - Experience with Next.js, Supabase, Vercel, or similar modern web stacks - Have shipped something, anything, built with AI assistance (show us) - Familiar with MCP, agent frameworks, or n8n / Zapier-style orchestration **How to apply** Do not send a generic cover letter. Send: 1. A link to one thing you built with AI help (even small — a script, a site, a Chrome extension) 2. A 3-5 sentence description of how you used AI to build it and what went wrong 3. Your favorite AI tool right now and why 4. The phrase "good vibes" in your application headline so we know you read this far 5. An intro video explaining who you are and your work Applications without these will be ignored. *We are building a long-term home for the right person. If you are looking for a stable, intellectually demanding role where you learn the cutting edge of AI engineering on the job, apply.*

title: Patient Navigation Specialist
description: Position Title: Patient Navigation Specialist Employment Type: Full-Time Department: Care Coordination / Patient Support Services Reports To: Operations Leadership / Care Management Leadership Company: United Chronic Care Management (UCCM) Position Overview: United Chronic Care Management (UCCM) is seeking a compassionate, patient-focused, and highly organized Patient Navigation Specialist to help patients transform assessment findings into clear, actionable plans that support their health and wellness goals. This role serves as a critical bridge between assessment and action. After patients complete their health assessments, the Patient Navigation Specialist works closely with them to identify priorities, establish meaningful goals, develop individualized care plans, and create a personalized "My Plan" that outlines the steps, services, and resources needed to achieve desired outcomes. The ideal candidate is an excellent communicator who is skilled at coaching, active listening, and patient engagement. This individual must be able to guide patients through goal-setting conversations, help them understand their care options, and develop practical action plans that align with their needs, preferences, and circumstances. This role is not simply documenting patient information—it is helping patients create a roadmap for success by turning assessment results into achievable goals, structured care plans, and coordinated next steps. Core Mission of the Role: To empower patients to take an active role in their health by developing personalized goals, creating comprehensive care plans, and guiding them through the next steps necessary to improve their health outcomes and overall well-being. Primary Responsibilities: - Care Plan Development Develop individualized care plans based on assessment findings and patient goals. Identify appropriate interventions, services, and support strategies to address patient needs. Ensure care plans are practical, achievable, and aligned with the patient's priorities. Regularly review and update care plans as patient needs and goals evolve. - Goal Setting Facilitate collaborative goal-setting conversations with patients. Help patients establish realistic, measurable, and meaningful short-term and long-term health goals. Assist patients in prioritizing goals based on their needs, readiness, and circumstances. Encourage accountability and patient ownership of their health journey. - My Plan Creation & Action Planning Create personalized "My Plan" documents that serve as a roadmap for each patient. Clearly outline patient goals, action steps, recommended services, follow-up activities, and expected outcomes. Educate patients on their care plans and ensure they understand their next steps. Help patients navigate and coordinate the services necessary to support their goals. - Documentation & Compliance Accurately document assessments, care plans, patient goals, progress notes, and follow-up activities. Maintain HIPAA compliance and patient confidentiality. Follow organizational policies, procedures, and quality standards. Contribute to continuous improvement efforts focused on patient engagement and outcomes. Desired Qualifications: Experience in healthcare, care coordination, patient navigation, health coaching, case management, or a related field. Strong communication, coaching, and motivational interviewing skills. Ability to build rapport and engage patients from diverse backgrounds. Strong organizational and documentation skills. Ability to develop structured care plans and action-oriented patient goals. Success in This Role Looks Like: Patients have clearly defined and measurable health goals. Personalized "My Plan" documents are completed accurately and on time. Care plans are actionable, patient-centered, and regularly updated. Patients understand their next steps and remain engaged in their care journey. Improved patient participation, adherence, and progress toward desired outcomes. Work Schedule Work hours are aligned with U.S. Eastern Time business operations. Specific shifts will be assigned during onboarding. IMPORTANT NOTE: Application Process Interested candidates should submit a current RESUME and a ONE-MINUTE VIDEO INTRODUCTION describing their experience communicating with U.S.-based customers or patients. Failure to submit any of these will not be considered. Qualified applicants will be contacted for the next steps in the selection process.

title: Billing Specialist

They are intelligent, capable people navigating a financial experience they were never trained for. They do not know what an evergreen retainer is. They do not know what a trust replenishment request means or why it matters. And if no one explains it in a way that makes sense to them, they lose confidence in the process, and they lose sight of the plan they are working toward. That is the problem this role solves. The Billing Specialist at Divorce With A Plan is the person who makes the financial side of a divorce case make sense to the client. You walk beside them from the day they retain the firm through the day the case closes, connecting every payment to the outcome they are working toward. You are part of their walk. You are the one who helps them see that the $5,000 retainer replenishment is not just a number. It is the next step toward the custody arrangement they need, the property division that protects their future, the agreement that lets them move forward. The time you spend with clients explaining their billing, answering their questions, and making sure their plan still makes sense to them is not an extra. It is not a favor. It is part of the service. There is no additional cost to the client for the time you invest in making sure they understand. That is how this firm works, and it is one of the reasons clients trust us. How we do it: the right way. This firm runs on structure. There is a defined process for everything, because when the process is clear, the client gets a consistent experience no matter which attorney is on their case or which week of the month it is. You will have a daily call block schedule so clients are never waiting days for a return call. You will have a billing script built on the Maryland Rules of Professional Conduct so clients hear accurate, compliant information every time. You will have an escalation protocol with documented timestamps, so no client concern sits unaddressed. You will have a weekly deliverable that captures how clients are feeling, what they need, and what feedback they are giving us, so the firm can respond to what clients are actually experiencing, not what we assume they are experiencing. If you are someone who finds relief in knowing exactly what the standard is, exactly what a good day looks like, and exactly what is expected, keep reading. What you produce: a contribution that protects the client and the firm. The Maryland Rules of Professional Conduct require that clients be kept informed about the status of their matter (Rule 1.4), that fees are reasonable and clearly communicated (Rule 1.5), and that client funds held in trust are safeguarded with precision (Rule 1.15). Those rules exist to protect the client. Everything this role does is built around upholding them. Every call you make either keeps a client informed or it does not. Every replenishment conversation either connects the payment to the client's goals and gives them the information they are entitled to, or it leaves them making financial decisions without the full picture. Every trust balance you monitor either gets flagged the same day it drops below threshold, protecting the client's funds and the firm's fiduciary obligation, or it becomes the kind of gap that puts both at risk. You are not here to process invoices. You are here to contribute to something that matters: a client's ability to get through the hardest financial experience of their life with clarity, dignity, and a plan that makes sense to them, while ensuring the fir ---------- ets the professional standards that make all of that possible. Here is who thrives in this role. You genuinely like people. Not in theory. In practice. You are energized by 20+ phone conversations a day because you actually want to know how someone is doing, and they can tell the difference. You remember that a client's daughter just started high school, that another client lost their job two months ago, that someone told you in March they were scared about the mediation in May, and when you call in May, you ask about it before you ask about the balance. You are organized because you cannot function without a system. You manage 100 to 150 active client relationships, and nothing falls through because you built something (a spreadsheet, a calendar, a color-coded tracker, a handwritten list) that keeps you moving. You do not wait for someone to tell you what needs attention. You see the attorney's calendar, you see the hearing in two weeks, and you pick up the phone, because the client deserves to know what is coming before it arrives. You have the emotional range to sit with a client who is crying about their financial situation on Tuesday and have a firm, direct conversation about a past-due balance on Wednesday, and both conversations are authentic because both come from the same place: you care about this person's outcome, and you are going to tell them the truth. You have been described as "the person who can get anyone to pay," and you know the reason is not pressure. It is trust. People pay you because you took the time to help them understand what they were paying for and why it mattered to their case. Here is who this role is not for. 1. If you want to process invoices in a back office and never talk to a client, this role will make you miserable. 2. If you avoid difficult conversations about money, you will not survive the first month. These clients are going through a divorce. Money is emotional. You need to be able to hold that space and still move the conversation forward, because the client needs someone who will stay in it with them. 3. If you need someone to tell you what to do every hour, this is not the right structure for you. You will have clear expectations, daily blocks, and weekly deliverables. Within that framework, you think, prioritize, and act. Problems get fixed or flagged, because a problem that sits is a client who waits. If you read from a script without understanding why each line exists, you will fail here. Every call requires context. You know what is happening in the client's case before you dial, and you lead with that, because a client who feels known is a client who stays engaged in their own plan. If the phrase "it has to make sense" does not resonate with you at a gut level, if you are comfortable with "good enough" or "that is just how we do it," you will not be happy working here. Responsibilities 1. Make the Financial Side of the Case Make Sense from Day One 2. Within five business days of retention, deliver a billing tutorial covering retainer structure, evergreen replenishment, invoice format, and what to expect at each stage, so the client starts their case understanding how the financial side works before they receive their first invoice. 3. Conduct a live introductory call to walk through the material, answer questions, and establish the relationship. This call gives the client a person they can reach when billing feels confusing, and it gives you the context to serve them well for the life of their case. 4. Provide specific dollar ranges for upcoming cost events (hearings: $5,000-$10,000, mediations, trials: $15,000-$30,000) so the client can plan ahead instead of reacting to surprises. 5. Introduce yourself as a non-billable point of contact. The time you spend making sure their plan still makes sense to them is part of the service, not an add-on. Clients who know they can call you without a meter running are clients who stay informed and engaged. 6. Keep Trust Accounts Funded by Keeping Clients Informed 7. Monitor trust balances daily across ---------- active matters so no client's case is disrupted by a funding gap they did not see coming. 8. Call every client before sending a replenishment request. No email goes out without a phone call attempt. The call comes first because the client deserves a conversation, not a demand. 9. When requesting additional retainers for upcoming events, reference the specific event by name and the date you first discussed it. This tells the client you are paying attention to their case, not just their balance. 10. Flag any matter below the trust threshold the same day. Not at the next billing cycle. The same day. A delay means the client's case could stall without warning. 11. Process Invoices the Right Way 12. Prepare, review, and distribute client invoices on a biweekly cycle, so clients receive accurate, consistent billing they can follow. 13. Review every time entry on every invoice for accuracy, specificity, and consistency. Flag entries that are vague, duplicative, or do not reflect the actual work performed, because a confusing invoice erodes the client's trust in the firm. 15. Contact timekeepers directly to resolve questionable entries before pre-bills go to attorneys. The client should never have to question whether an entry is real. 17. Distribute finalized invoices on the scheduled date with payment links included so clients always know what they owe and how to pay without chasing anyone down. 18. Collect by Connecting Payment to Progress 19. Maintain accounts receivable below 2% of total billings. 20. Execute 12-15 outbound calls per day during the morning AR block, with every call documented in Clio so the client's history is always current if another tea ---------- mber needs to step in. 21. Lead every collections conversation with a case update: what was accomplished, what is upcoming, and how the work connects to the client's goal. The client hears the value before they hear the number. 22. When a client says they cannot pay, walk through every option: credit cards, personal loans, family support, employer assistance, and legal fee financing. You do not accept "I cannot" without helping them look at every door first, because a client who feels they have no options may abandon a case they still need. 23. Send payment links the same day after any commitment so the client can act while the conversation is fresh. 24. Listen, Learn, and Report What Clients Need Pay attention to what clients tell you on every call. Their questions, their frustrations, their confusion, and their feedback are data the firm needs to hear so we can serve them better. 25. Produce a weekly deliverable every Friday, capturing client feedback, recurring questions, unresolved needs, and what you are hearing about the client experience. This is how the firm stays connected to what clients actually need instead of guessing. 26. When a billing concern arises, log it with a documented timestamp and route it to the responsible attorney via email so the client gets a response, not silence. 27. Escalate any concern involving bar grievance, fraud, or legal action language to firm leadership the same day, because those situations require immediate attention to protect the client and the firm. 28. Stay Ahead of the Attorneys Check attorney calendars for upcoming hearings, mediations, and trials. Initiate additional retainer requests before anyone asks, so the client has time to prepare instead of scrambling. 29. Confirm all credits, write-offs, and billing holds in writing before any related bill is finalized. If a credit is pending and you are not certain it has been applied, hold the bill. A client should never receive an invoice that does not reflect what the firm already knows. 30. Document every retainer reduction, billing pause, or special instruction in Clio at the matter level the same day so the next person who touches the file has the full picture and the client never has to repeat themselves. Qualifications Required: • 2+ years in billing, collections, or accounts receivable in a professional services environment. Law firm experience strongly preferred. • High comfort with outbound phone calls and client-facing conversations. This role requires 20+ calls per day. If phones drain you, this is not the right fit. • Proficiency with practice management software (Clio Manage preferred, or ability to learn within 30 days). • Ability to read and interpret legal invoices, time entries, trust account statements, and engagement agreements. • Strong written communication for documented escalations, client correspondence, and weekly deliverables. • Proficiency with Google Workspace (Gmail, Sheets, Calendar, Drive). • Demonstrated ability to manage 100+ active relationships simultaneously without dropping threads. Training provided, but baseline awareness accelerates onboarding. • Experience with evergreen retainer models and trust accounting. • Prior use of LawPay, Dialpad, or Clio Grow. • Bilingual (English/Spanish) is a plus. Appointment Setter / Sales Pipeline Owner — DTC SEO Agency Type: Full-time, remote. Must work US Central business hours (we're based in Austin, TX). Non-negotiable. Reports to: Thomas (fixed weekly 15-min scorecard review). Day-to-day, you own your own numbers in the tracker; the tracker is the accountability mechanism. Comp: Flat base at your quoted monthly rate. Commitment: Long-term. This is not a 3-month gig; we want someone who grows with the company. Why this role exists: Right now inbound leads go un-worked, booked calls no-show, reschedules get dropped, and two-plus years of previous leads sit untouched across old CRMs. This role owns everything between "a lead exists" and "Thomas is on the call," then fills downtime with partner outreach. You own this pipeline; you don't wait to be told. 1. Speed-to-lead (daily, time-critical) Text and call every new inbound within 5 minutes during working hours. Pre-qualify against the qualified-call standard (below). Get them excited to talk to Thomas as an SEO expert. Book qualified leads straight onto Thomas's calendar. 2. Calendar & booking authority Own Thomas's sales calendar. Load his availability live on calls and book the time directly. Authority to move and reschedule bookings to keep the slate full and pull calls earlier (closer booking = higher show rate). 3. Show-rate protection Confirm every booked call twice (24h and 1h prior) by text/call. Standard: every confirmable call gets confirmed, no exceptions. Where a call is booked far out, work to pull it earlier. 4. Reschedule recovery (daily, zero-drop) Any lead who asks to reschedule gets called/texted the same day to lock a new time. No reschedule sits unanswered. 5. Reactivation (front-loaded first weeks, then ongoing) Work previous leads across all old CRMs: GHL funnel, dormant iClosed leads, ClickUp audited-but-unclosed clients. Re-engage and book onto Thomas's calendar. Audit angle: "we ran your audit a while back, things have likely changed, worth a fresh look with Thomas?" This is gold sitting untouched; treat it as a priority, not a someday task. 6. Pre-call prep Before each discovery call, research the lead: website, LinkedIn, revenue signals, current SEO state. Hand Thomas a one-page brief so he walks in fully prepped. 7. Funnel optimization (ownership, not just execution) Own the SendBlue text and Gmail email sequences for inbound and booked leads. Plug the unbooked-lead gap (form-fillers who don't book currently get nothing). Build a 3-touch sequence (text, email , text over ~5 days). Test variants of the opener text to lift reply rate; bring 2-3 versions with reasoning, not just "send more." Sharpen the pre-call email series to build show-up urgency and lightly re-qualify. Flag where an automated message should become a manual personal touch (or vice versa). Judge all changes on the numbers: opener reply rate, show rate, book rate. 8. Onboarding handoff (on close) When Thomas closes a client: grab the Fathom link, set up the ClickUp folder, alert the team to start. 9. Partner outreach (downtime / overflow capacity) Find agencies, consultants, and heads of growth serving $5M+ DTC ecommerce brands. Reach out via email and LinkedIn; book them onto Thomas's calendar. Pitch and book Thomas as a guest on the partner's podcast where relevant (gives the partner value, builds the relationship). Send Thomas's weekly YouTube video to the partner DB as a recurring top-of-mind touch; log it. 10. Tracker ownership (ongoing) Build and maintain the single source of truth for every lead and partner: source, stage, last contact, next action, owner. Current and accurate at all times. Nothing lives in anyone's head. 11. Calling stack setup (week 1 task) Set up and test the web-app dialer with Krisp accent converter. Confirm live-call quality and latency. If Krisp doesn't cut it, find and test an alternative. This is yours to own. Qualified call standard (a lead only reaches Thomas's calendar if ALL are true): Ecommerce brand (hard requirement) $5M+ annual revenue (ICP), or $1M+ with clear budget Product-market fit: real product, real demand Scaling profitably with paid ads Sub-$1M or unqualified leads get routed to partners or disqualified. Booking unqualified leads to pad the count is the one way to fail this role while looking busy. KPIs (tracked weekly, these define whether the job is being done): Speed-to-lead: 90%+ of inbound contacted within 5 min (working hours) 5 qualified calls booked per week from reactivation Show rate: 85-90% of booked calls held; every confirmable call confirmed twice Reschedules recovered same-day: 100% Partner conversations booked for Thomas: monthly target (feeds the ~20 partnerships/mo goal) Tracker current at every weekly review These aren't bonus targets, they're the standard. Clearing them keeps the seat; missing them consistently triggers the 30-day kill criteria. Tools: iClosed (booking), SendBlue (texts), web-app dialer + Krisp (calls), GHL, ClickUp, Gmail, LinkedIn, Fathom. Must-haves: US Central hours (non-negotiable). Fluent, natural spoken English. Phone-confident and able to pre-qualify. Self-directed; owns a tracker without reminders. Appointment-setting or phone sales experience. Hungry, long-term, goes above the bare minimum.

title: Executive Operations Assistant
description: About the Business We are a Florida-focused curative title real estate investing company. We work on properties with complicated ownership, probate, heirship, tax, lien, and title issues. Our business depends on clean follow-through, accurate documents, organized files, consistent communication, and disciplined execution from signed purchase agreement through attorney handoff, probate progress, document completion, and closing readiness. Role Overview This is not a generic virtual assistant role. We are looking for a calm, steady, detail-driven Executive Operations Assistant who can become the operational control point for the COO. The right person will keep the COO organized, coordinate transaction and notary workflows, monitor probate case progress, maintain complete deal files, and audit documents before key handoffs. You should enjoy structure, checklists, clean folders, accurate notes, careful follow-up, and quiet execution. You do not need to be loud, salesy, or highly social. You do need to be reliable, precise, patient, consistent, and comfortable holding people accountable to next steps. Core Responsibilities 1. Executive Assistant to the COO • Protect the COO’s time by organizing priorities, reminders, follow-ups, meetings, and action items. • Prepare daily priority lists, meeting notes, agendas, and post-meeting task summaries. • Monitor assigned inboxes, messages, calendars, documents, and task lists for urgent items and missed follow-ups. • Turn verbal instructions into clear written tasks, checklists, and next actions. • Maintain calm, professional communication while supporting a fast-moving operator. 2. Transaction / Notary / Closing Coordination • Coordinate mobile notary appointments with sellers, heirs, and notaries after purchase agreements are signed. • Prepare and organize signing packages, notary instructions, FedEx labels, tracking links, and scanback requirements. • Track execution of Joinders, Quitclaim Deeds, Assignments of Interest, Affidavits of Heirs, copies of IDs, and related documents. • Review scanbacks for completeness before forwarding packages to the proper internal tea ---------- mber, probate attorney, or closing-related party. • Maintain transaction status, next steps, blockers, and deadlines in the CRM/project management system. 3. Probate Case Coordination • Monitor probate-related deal progress and maintain case status updates. • Communicate with probate attorneys and internal tea ---------- mbers to track what is pending, filed, missing, signed, recorded, or ready for next action. • Maintain open-items lists for each probate file, including missing heirs, missing documents, pending attorney tasks, and court/status updates. • Organize probate documents, attorney correspondence, family/heir notes, and supporting evidence in the correct folders. • Escalate stalled cases before they become forgotten cases. 4. Deal File Management / Curative File Control • Keep every deal file clean, complete, and easy to understand. • Maintain digital folders, naming conventions, document checklists, title issue notes, heir charts, seller information, and transaction records. • Ensure each file has a clear current status, next action, responsible person, and due date. • Prepare clean handoff packages for attorneys, title companies, internal reviewers, or closing coordination. • Prevent scattered information, duplicate documents, missing IDs, incorrect versions, and unclear file history. 5. Quality Control / Document Audit • Audit documents before signing, after scanback, before attorney handoff, and before title/closing handoff. • Check names, dates, signatures, notarizations, legal descriptions, attachments, IDs, missing pages, and consistency across documents. • Flag issues clearly and early instead of assuming someone else will catch them. • Maintain QC checklists and document audit logs. • Help the team reduce costly errors, closing delays, and repeated requests to sellers or heirs. The Person Who Will Thrive in This Role • You are calm under pressure and do not need constant excitement to stay engaged. • You naturally create order out of scattered information. • You are comfortable with repetitive follow-up, checklists, and status tracking. • You notice small details that other people miss. • You are professional, direct, and respectful when following up with sellers, notaries, attorneys, and internal tea ---------- mbers. • You can manage up: if the COO misses a decision, deadline, or open item, you will respectfully bring it back to the front. • You prefer accuracy over speed, but you can still move quickly when the process is clear. • You are loyal, stable, consistent, and serious about long-term work. This Role Is Probably Not a Fit If... • You need a highly social, chatty, people-heavy role to feel energized. • You dislike repetitive checklists, document review, file organization, or administrative follow-through. • You prefer improvising over following a proven process. • You get bored when the work requires precision, patience, and consistency. • You avoid following up because you do not want to bother people. • You are uncomfortable working behind the scenes in a support and coordination role. • You want a sales, negotiation, or lead-generation role instead of an operations support role. Required Skills and Experience • Excellent written English and professional communication skills. • Strong organization, task tracking, and file management ability. • High attention to detail when reviewing names, documents, dates, IDs, signatures, and instructions. • Comfortable using CRMs, Google Drive, Google Sheets, email , calendars, messaging tools, and project/task systems. • Ability to work Central Time Zone hours consistently. • Reliable internet connection and quiet work environment. • Experience as an Executive Assistant, Transaction Coordinator, Legal Assistant, Real Estate VA, Probate Assistant, Title Assistant, or Operations Coordinator is preferred. • Experience with U.S. real estate, probate, legal documents, notary coordination, or title-related work is a strong advantage, but trainability and accuracy matter most. Tools You May Use • Pipedrive or similar CRM • Google Workspace: Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Calendar • Phone/messaging systems such as Quo, WhatsApp, or similar • Project/task management tools • FedEx label and tracking workflows • Shared digital folders and document checklists Success Metrics • No unsigned, missing, or incomplete document packages sent forward without being flagged. • Every active transaction has a current status, next step, owner, and due date. • Notary appointments, FedEx labels, scanbacks, attorney handoffs, and follow-ups are tracked without gaps. • Probate cases do not stall silently; blockers are identified and escalated. • Deal files are clean, organized, and ready for review at any time. • The COO has fewer dropped balls, fewer reminders to give, and more operational visibility. First 30/60/90 Days - Timeframe & Expected Progress First 30 Days Learn the business model, tools, document types, folder structure, transaction workflow, and daily communication rhythm. Begin supporting COO priorities and tracking simple tasks. First 60 Days Own notary coordination, scanback tracking, deal file organization, and basic QC checklists with supervision. Begin maintaining probate status trackers and open-items lists. First 90 Days Operate as the daily control point for COO support, transaction coordination, probate tracking, file hygiene, and document audit workflows. Identify process gaps and help improve SOPs. Schedule and Compensation • $5/hour starting compensation plus deal bonuses. • Central Time Zone working hours required. • Long-term opportunity for someone who becomes dependable, accurate, and deeply trusted. • Deal bonuses are tied to successful transaction progress and closed deals, based on internal company policy. How to Apply To apply, reply with the subject line: "Executive Operations Assistant - Detail Control" and include the following: 1. A short paragraph explaining why you are a strong fit for a detail-heavy operations support role. 2. Your experience with executive assistance, transaction coordination, real estate, legal documents, probate, title, notary coordination, or file management. 3. A specific example of a time you caught a small detail that prevented a bigger problem. 4. A specific example of how you track multiple open tasks, deadlines, and follow-ups. 5. Your availability in Central Time Zone hours. 6. Your internet speed, computer setup, and whether you have a quiet work environment. 7. Confirm that you are comfortable with $5/hour plus deal bonuses. 8.     Provide DISC test results: ---------- /disc-personality-test/ 9.     Copy of resume. Small Detail Test At the end of your application, write this exact sentence: "I understand that this role requires calm consistency, accurate follow-up, and clean files." Applications that do not follow the instructions above may not be reviewed. This role is for someone who pays close attention to details before the job even begins.

title: Head of Contact Center Operations - Remote
job_title: Head of Contact Center Operations - Remote
description: Company Overview The Compliance Services Organization didn't exist. We built it. MP1 Solutions pioneered the Compliance Services Organization (CSO) — a new category of operating partner built to replace the fragmented vendor model that has defined compliance programs for decades. Built on the foundation of MedPro Disposal, the nation's largest privately-held medical waste company serving 35,000+ providers across 48 states over the past 15 years, MP1 Solutions extends that operational infrastructure, vendor network, and customer trust into a category we're actively building — and leading. We're doing it with a technology-forward approach, actively developing the AI infrastructure that will make this model smarter, faster, and more scalable as we grow. What we do: We operate as the single compliance partner for non-acute healthcare facilities — consolidating every obligation into one coordinated program, assigning one dedicated account manager as the point of accountability, and actively managing the underlying vendor ecosystem through continuous evaluation, negotiation, and optimization on the practice's behalf. Why it matters: Regulated facilities across the country are managing compliance the same fragmented way they always have. We're changing that — and we're looking for people who want to help build what comes next. Our technology: We're actively building the AI infrastructure that sits behind this model — automating compliance tracking, surfacing risks before they become problems, and creating a system that gets smarter with every client we add. If you want to build at the intersection of compliance and technology, you're in the right place. Our impact: Our clients never have to worry about something falling through the cracks — obligations are coordinated, tracked, and documented in one place. We audit costs, eliminate overcharges, and deliver proof of compliance that always keeps practices inspection ready. Every client has one dedicated account manager who owns their program end to end. And unlike a traditional vendor relationship, our model is designed to get better over time — continuously re-evaluated, optimized, and improved with every client we serve. Position Overview: The Head of Contact Center Operations is the senior execution leader of MedPro and MP1's contact center — the person who makes the operation run, improves it continuously, and manages the managers who manage the floor. You report to the VP of Operations and translate their strategic direction into daily operational reality. This role sits at the intersection of operator and thought partner. You have done this before: run high-volume, multi-channel service environments, built capacity plans between labor and systems, designed operating models from the ground up, and led teams through system migrations without losing service continuity. You are not here to hold the org steady — you are here to elevate it. Where the VP of Operations sets the vision, you own delivery. When the VP of Operations needs to present performance to the COO, the data, the narrative, and the operational confidence behind it come from you. When the organization needs its service processes redesigned, its CRM environment assessed, or its team structure rebuilt — that work belongs to you. Key Responsibilities: Multi-Layer Team Leadership & People Development • Lead, coach, and develop Operations Managers and Team Leads — you manage the managers, and they manage the floor. Build leaders who build others. • Establish clear performance expectations, coaching cadences, and accountability frameworks across all leadership levels — weekly 1:1s, call calibrations, structured performance reviews, and real-time feedback loops. • Drive workforce planning and capacity modeling: design the right staffing structure between labor, channels, and volume patterns — not just fill headcount, but engineer capacity. • Build succession plans and internal development pathways that reduce external hiring dependency and create a promotion pipeline from within. • Own recruitment strategy for the operations team in partnership with HR — attract, hire, and retain the caliber of leader and frontline talent that the CSO model demands. • Foster a performance culture aligned to MedPro's values: Do the Right Thing, Figure It Out, Win as a Team, and Accountability & Ownership. Operating Model Design & Service Delivery • Assess the current state of the contact center operation — people, process, structure, channels, and systems — and translate findings into a clear-eyed redesign plan with sequenced priorities. • Design and implement the operating model: how the team is structured, how work flows through channels, how performance is governed, and how the organization scales as the client base grows. • Own day-to-day operational performance across all service channels — inbound and outbound voice, email , chat, and SMS — with direct accountability for SLA attainment, handle time, first-contact resolution, and quality scores. • Build and maintain the full SOP and playbook library: every process documented, auditable, and owned. If it is not written down, it does not exist. • Own the quality assurance framework — define rubrics, conduct or oversee audits, deliver structured coaching feedback to leads, and use quality data to drive continuous improvement. • Manage real-time workload distribution across channels — monitor queues, adjust staffing deployment as volume shifts, and act on performance signals without waiting to be asked. System Assessment & Service Technology Migration • Conduct a thorough assessment of the current CRM and service technology environment — understanding what exists, what is working, what is limiting, and what migration path forward best serves the operation. • Lead the end-to-end service system migration: requirements gathering, vendor evaluation, workflow configuration, data mapping, agent training, parallel testing, and go-live — while maintaining service continuity throughout. • Design and configure case management workflows, escalation paths, SLA tracking, and omni-channel routing logic in the new system, aligned to MedPro's service model and client base. • Partner with the internal technology team to ensure all system integrations — IVR handoffs, client account data, ticketing — flow cleanly from day one. • Build post-migration operating model documentation: how cases are created, routed, resolved, escalated, and reported — so no process lives in someone's head. • Drive full agent and Team Lead adoption: training materials, live coaching sessions, compliance monitoring, and performance metrics in the new system until it is the single active system of record. • Design, build, and maintain IVR call flows that intelligently route clients, reduce handle time, and improve containment — build these, not just manage ones that already exist. Performance Management, Data & Reporting • Own the KPI framework — define the right metrics, build the dashboards, and drive accountability systems that make performance visible and improvable at every level of the team. • Deliver structured weekly and monthly performance reports to the VP of Operations — covering channel SLA attainment, CSAT trends, quality scores, case volume, and system migration status. • Translate floor-level data into operational decisions and clear narrative: what is driving variance, what specific action will improve it, and what the risk is if it is not addressed. • Communicate proactively to the VP of Operations about service risks, capacity issues, and migration blockers — full transparency, solution-first framing, no surprises that should have been visible earlier. • Identify and scope AI-assist and automation opportunities (IVR containment, agent-assist prompts, chatbot deflection) — bring the VP of Operations a prioritized business case, not just ideas. Client Experience & Regulatory Compliance • Own the client experience at the operational level — serving as the escalation point for complex service issues and ensuring every client interaction reflects MedPro and MP1's positioning as a true compliance partner. • Map and continuously improve the client journey across all contact touchpoints — identifying friction, closing gaps, and driving measurable improvements in client satisfaction scores. • Ensure operational adherence to all applicable data security, privacy, and healthcare regulatory requirements including HIPAA and related standards. • Partner with Sales and Client Success to align operational delivery with client growth, renewal, and expansion strategies. Qualifications: Required • 10–15 years of total experience in contact center operations, service delivery, or BPO leadership — with significant, demonstrable accountability for team performance, service transformation, and operational change. • Minimum 5 years in a senior people-management role with direct accountability for multi-layer teams (managers managing managers), department-level KPIs, and operational planning. Candidates who have only managed frontline teams — and not managed managers — will not be a fit. • Proven experience operating in high-volume, multi-channel service environments with large numbers of customer interactions across voice, email , chat, and digital touchpoints. This is an execution role — we need someone who has run the floor at volume, not just designed programs from above it. • Demonstrated experience leading a service system migration in a live contact center — transitioning a team from a legacy CRM to a modern platform while maintaining service continuity. Salesforce Service Cloud experience is strongly preferred. • Hands-on capacity planning expertise: ability to model the right labor structure against channel mix, volume forecasts, and SLA requirements — and build the operating model that delivers it. • Deep IVR design and multi-channel routing experience — you have built IVR flows from scratch, configured routing logic, and measured containment impact. • Strong analytical capability — builds and interprets dashboards, identifies performance drivers, and communicates findings clearly to senior leadership. • Exceptional written and verbal English communication skills for daily interaction with U.S.-based leadership. • Background in healthcare BPO, compliance services, regulated service industries, or U.S.-facing contact center operations strongly preferred. Nice-to-Have • Salesforce Service Cloud proficiency — case management, workflow rules, SLA configuration, omni-channel routing, and reporting. • Experience with AI-assist tools in contact center settings: agent-assist prompts, chatbot deflection, predictive routing. • Workforce management platform experience (NICE IEX, Verint, Calabrio, or similar). • HIPAA familiarity and/or exposure to U.S. healthcare regulatory compliance operations. • Track record of building or rebuilding operations within a high-growth or category-defining company. • Six Sigma, COPC, or equivalent contact center quality certification. Compensation & Benefits: • Salary Range: $18-$24/hr • Permanent work-from-home • 40 hours per week, aligned with U.S. business hours (CST, graveyard shift). • Fixed weekends off (Saturday & Sunday) • Work Anniversary Bonus • No work with pay on US Holidays • Paid Leaves after 6 months of employment! Basic Technical Requirements: • Your own laptop/desktop PC with the following minimum specs: i5 5th gen and above/AMD equivalent; 8GB RAM; Mozilla or Chrome installed; Windows 10 upwards. • A consistent and stable internet connection of at least 20Mbps • With back-up computer, internet connection and power supply • Noise-canceling headset/headphones • A quiet and dedicated workspace at home Application Process: 1. title: Heir Outreach Specialist
description: We are hiring a confident, persuasive, and highly proactive Heir Outreach Specialist to help our real estate investment company contact property owners and heirs connected to distressed Florida properties. This is not a passive admin role. This role is for someone who enjoys starting conversations, moving people to action, asking direct questions, and staying calm when a family situation is complicated. Our business solves title problems involving inherited property, probate issues, tax deed risk, liens, judgments, and family ownership problems. Your job is to help us reach the right heirs, confirm family relationships, gather key facts, build trust quickly, and keep communication moving so our acquisitions and transaction teams can close deals. What You Will Do • Call, text, and follow up with heirs and property owners connected to inherited or distressed Florida real estate. • Start conversations confidently with people who may not be expecting your call. • Identify decision-makers inside families with multiple heirs, siblings, children, spouses, or extended relatives. • Ask clear fact-finding questions about family relationships, deceased owners, probate status, property history, occupancy, and seller motivation. • Build rapport quickly while still keeping the conversation focused and productive. • Overcome hesitation and confusion without being pushy, rude, or robotic. • Document every conversation accurately inside our CRM so the rest of the team knows exactly what happened and what needs to happen next. • Coordinate warm handoffs to the acquisitions team when a seller or heir is ready to discuss an offer. • Persistently follow up until the family situation is understood, the right person is reached, or the lead is properly disqualified. Who This Role Is Perfect For • You are naturally confident on the phone and do not freeze when someone is guarded, confused, emotional, or skeptical. • You like winning conversations, solving people puzzles, and figuring out who has authority inside a family. • You are comfortable being direct, but you know how to sound respectful and human. • You move fast, follow up aggressively, and do not need to be reminded five times to complete the next step. • You prefer clear goals, measurable results, and real responsibility over repetitive low-impact admin work. • You can handle messy information, incomplete family trees, and leads where the first person you reach is not the final decision-maker. • You are energized by the challenge of turning cold or lukewarm contacts into productive conversations. You Will Not Be a Fit If • You are uncomfortable making outbound calls or speaking with strangers. • You need every step scripted before you can take action. • You avoid difficult conversations or give up after one unanswered call. • You are careless with notes, names, dates, phone numbers, or relationship details. • You sound overly timid, overly formal, or robotic on the phone. • You prefer back-office data entry and do not want to be accountable for outreach results. Required Skills • Strong spoken English with a clear, confident, professional phone presence. • Experience with outbound calling, sales, appointment setting, customer service, collections, real estate, legal intake, probate, or lead follow-up is strongly preferred. • Ability to ask questions, listen carefully, and control the direction of a conversation. • Comfortable using CRM systems, spreadsheets, Google Workspace, WhatsApp, and phone software. • Fast and accurate note-taking after calls and text conversations. • Stable internet connection, quiet work environment, and reliable computer. • High ownership: you follow through without needing constant supervision. Real Estate / Probate Experience You do not need to be an expert in Florida probate or curative title work before starting. We will train the right person on our lead types, terminology, workflows, and CRM process. However, you must be a fast learner, comfortable with complex family situations, and willing to study the business so you can improve quickly. Performance Expectations • Make consistent outbound calls, texts, and follow-ups during assigned work hours. • Reach heirs, confirm relationships, and identify the right decision-makers. • Maintain clean CRM records after every meaningful interaction. • Move qualified leads forward quickly instead of letting them sit idle. • Communicate daily progress, blockers, and next-step recommendations to the team. • Demonstrate measurable improvement in call quality, contact rate, lead qualification, and handoffs over time. Training and Support • Call scripts, talk tracks, and objection-handling guidance. • Training on inherited property, heirs, probate-related terminology, and title problems. • CRM workflow training and lead status definitions. • Daily or weekly coaching based on actual calls, notes, and results. • Clear success metrics so you always know what winning looks like. Work Schedule This role requires availability during U.S. calling hours. Exact schedule can be discussed, but strong candidates should be available for meaningful overlap with Central Time business hours. Consistent attendance, responsiveness, and daily execution are required. Compensation $5/hr + $250 bonus per deal closed How to Apply To apply, send an email to ---------- with the subject line: “Heir Outreach - I Can Move Leads Forward” • A short summary of your outbound calling, sales, real estate, legal, probate, collections, or lead follow-up experience. • A 60- to 90-second voice recording introducing yourself and explaining why you would be effective in this role. • Your available work hours in Central Time. • DISC test results: ---------- • A brief answer to this question: “Tell me about a time you had to keep following up with someone who was hard to reach. What did you do?” Applications without a voice recording, specified DISC test results, and the required subject line may not be reviewed.

You'll have the opportunity to contribute ideas, influence our visual direction, and help shape how our brand is presented. Your work will appear across social media, articles, websites, presentations, lead magnets, advertising campaigns, and other marketing initiatives. The ideal designer: * Has an exceptional eye for typography, layout, composition, and visual hierarchy * Can communicate ideas visually—not just decorate a page * Produces polished, professional work with excellent attention to detail * Manages multiple projects and deadlines effectively * Communicates clearly and works well independently * Enjoys learning new tools and continually improving their craft * Uses AI to enhance creativity and productivity—not replace thoughtful design * Wants to make a meaningful contribution as part of a collaborative team Experience with Adobe Illustrator, Photoshop, Figma, Canva Pro, Adobe Express, or similar design tools is preferred. If you have an idea that helps us better serve our clients or strengthen our brand, we want to hear it. We value people who think critically, respectfully challenge assumptions, and take ownership of their work. The best ideas can come from anyone on our team. Our goal isn't simply to produce more graphics. It's to continually elevate the quality of our brand, create visual content that genuinely helps our clients succeed, and build marketing that stands out for all the right reasons. If you're looking for repetitive production work where someone tells you exactly what to do every day, this probably isn't the right position. If you're excited about becoming a creative contributor who helps shape our visual identity, contributes new ideas, and takes pride in producing exceptional work, we'd love to meet you. --- ## What Success Looks Like Success in this role isn't measured by how many graphics you produce. It's measured by the impact those graphics have. I tested a simple query: "Where can I buy books or merch?" The message appeared in the chat, but I did not observe a follow-up A.I. answer during the test window. description: Job Title: Blog-to-Reel Storyteller — Chic Kitty + Shaggy Chic ($9/video, Ongoing) Type: Gig Wage/Salary: $9 per finished Reel 3 Skills: Video Editing · Social Media Video Editing · Video Content Creation Blog-to-Reel Storyteller — Chic Kitty + Shaggy Chic (Gig, Ongoing) — $9/video Job Type: Gig, paid per video, ongoing Pay: $9 per finished Reel Initial gig: 30 Reels, delivered and paid in gated steps — 5, then 10, then 15 Ongoing: minimum 30 Reels every 3 weeks, at your pace, in two batches of 15 (evenly split cats and dogs) Company: Chic Kitty / Shaggy Chic — a pet lifestyle media company ABOUT THIS WORK We run two editorial pet lifestyle brands — Chic Kitty (cats) and Shaggy Chic (dogs).  We give you one of our blog posts; you turn its storyline into a beautifully crafted, visually engaging, educational, and luxurious short-form video.  The blog is your script. This is gig work, paid per video, ongoing for the right editor. This is not for people who film their pets and hope.  This is storytelling: a clear hook, a narrative built from the blog, completion-optimized, editorial grade. BRAND VOICE AND LOOK (read this — it is the whole job) None of our brands is cute or cutesy — we are the opposite.   Animals are revered family members and intelligent subjects, never "the cat/dog," "fur baby," "pet," or "cute." We talk to our audience. Chic Kitty (cats): "the cat lover's edit" — elevated, quiet, observational, intelligent.  Calm and editorial, the cat is treated with real respect. Shaggy Chic (dogs): "life, styled with dogs" — warm, refined, east-coast lifestyle. References for the feel: Kinfolk, Aesop, The Row, a Vogue editorial.  Luxurious restraint, not flash. THE DELIVERABLE Short-form vertical videos built from the blog we give you (the storyline and script) plus premium licensed stock (Artgrid + Storyblocks, or your own premium libraries). We do not provide brand footage. One clear narrative per video, drawn from the blog Educational and luxurious — the viewer should learn something and feel the quality PRODUCTION STANDARDS (firm) Format: 9:16 vertical, 1080×1920 MP4 Length: 10–20 seconds; aim 10–15 Hook: strongest ---------- nt or clearest promise in the first 1–3 seconds Color grade: cool/neutral editorial — warm or golden grades are an automatic no; no heavy filters Loop: end frame flows cleanly back to the opening No burned-in text — our team adds captions No watermarks of any kind, from any app Audio: do not deliver silently. Deliver with rich sound — ASMR or natural sound, and/or a U.S. trending-style audio bed that fits the story.  (We may swap the final trending track in-app at post.) 100% human editing, no AI-generated footage or subject.  Hard rule, we screen for it. REVISIONS AND QUALITY GATE One revision round is included per video — we flag anything off-spec, you fix it The initial gig is gated so we both know it is a fit: deliver 5, approved, paid, then 10, approved, paid, then 15, approved, paid .Ongoing: 30 every 3 weeks in two batches of 15, paid per video on approved delivery of each batch Quality is the only thing that earns more —consistently missing spec after a revision round ends the engagement. LOGISTICS Remote, ongoing, at your pace (minimum 30 every 3 weeks) Viewer access to blogs and briefs via our secure Drive; files named according to our convention Paid per video via Remitly on approved delivery Reports to the Operations Manager for handoff and review TO APPLY Share 2–3 short-form vertical videos you personally edited (links) — storytelling/editorial preferred. We give you a blog titled "The quiet signs your cat trusts you." What is your hook in the first 1–3 seconds, and how do you build a 12–15s educational story from it? Which stock libraries do you use, and how do you keep footage from looking generic? How do you approach sound — ASMR versus a trending audio bed — for a calm, luxurious pet video? Paid sample: finalists edit one Reel from a blog as a paid sample ($9, paid whether or not we proceed).  This protects both of us. We read every application. Generic or AI-written responses will not move forward.

If you are detail-obsessed, thrive on organizing chaos, and enjoy working with AI tools instead of being threatened by them, this role is for you. This is a full-time, long-term remote role with strong overlap required with US Eastern time. Core Responsibilities Multi-inbox email management * Own end-to-end management of multiple Gmail/Google Workspace inboxes (business, personal-business, and project-specific). * Triage all incoming email s: categorize, label, and prioritize based on context (investors, partners, vendors, internal, transactional, personal, etc.). * Use AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Copilot, other assistants) to generate draft responses, then edit for accuracy, tone, and context before sending or surfacing for approval. * Maintain a robust system of filters, labels, folders, and rules that works consistently across all inboxes. * Ensure no important email goes unanswered or unnoticed; monitor SLAs (e.g., everything acknowledged within 24 hours unless explicitly deferred). * Proactively unsubscribe, archive, and clean noise while protecting newsletters and sources I explicitly value. Multi-calendar ownership * Own multiple Google Calendars for a single executive (work, personal, portfolio/board, and travel-related calendars). * Schedule, confirm, and reschedule meetings across all calendars so that time is used intentionally and conflicts are prevented. * Coordinate across time zones with internal teams, external partners, investors, and travel-related contacts. * Protect focus time and deep work blocks while balancing meetings, travel, and personal requirements. * Prepare daily and weekly calendar briefs with context for each meeting (who they are, why we’re meeting, what outcome we want). * Ensure that travel, buffer times, and recurring commitments are accurately represented across all calendars. Travel, logistics, and preferences * Support business travel planning: identify options, prepare shortlists, and finalize bookings for flights, hotels, and ground transportation in alignment with preferences. * Build structured itineraries that align calendar events with bookings, confirmation numbers, time zones, and contact details. * Track loyalty programs, common routes, preferred hotel brands, and seating preferences, and factor them into recommendations. * Handle changes, delays, and last-minute adjustments with minimal disruption to the overall schedule. AI, systems, and workflow optimization * Use AI assistants to draft email s, summarize threads, prepare meeting notes, and create briefings for upcoming calls. * Help design and maintain clear operating systems for email and calendar management across all accounts (e.g., labels, status tags, “for review,” “awaiting reply,” “archive by default”). * Identify repetitive patterns and collaborate on automations (e.g., filters, templates, Zapier/Make workflows) that reduce manual work while preserving judgment and control. * Keep simple documentation of workflows and decision rules so the system is repeatable and improvable over time. Operational and executive support * Track action items that emerge from email s and meetings and ensure follow-through, including nudging me and other stakeholders when needed. * Perform targeted research (e.g., vendors, tools, travel options, prospect/company background before meetings) and synthesize into concise briefs. * Maintain organized digital documents and links relevant to ongoing projects (e.g., in Google Docs/Drive, Notion, or similar). * Support occasional personal-business tasks that intersect with my professional world (e.g., memberships, events, conferences). You’re a great fit if you * Have 2+ years supporting a senior executive remotely, with heavy emphasis on inbox and calendar management. * Have demonstrable experience managing multiple inboxes and calendars for one decision-maker (not just a single account). * Are highly organized, systems-oriented, and comfortable designing and following structured processes. * Write clear, concise, professional English and can reliably refine AI-generated drafts so they sound human, thoughtful, and aligned with guidance. * Are comfortable using Google Workspace (Gmail, Calendar, Drive) and modern SaaS/communication tools; familiarity with AI tools is a plus. * Can understand enough technical context (APIs, cloud, SaaS, travel tech) to categorize and prioritize messages intelligently, even if you are not an engineer. * Exercise strong judgment regarding what you can handle directly vs. what needs my input, and when to escalate something quickly. * Are proactive and anticipatory — you are thinking one or two steps ahead on email , calendar, and logistics. * Can reliably overlap with US Eastern business hours (at least 6–8 hours of overlap). Bonus points * Experience supporting a CTO, VP Engineering, or founder in technology, SaaS, or travel tech. * Familiarity with tools like Jira/Confluence, Notion, Slack, or similar collaboration platforms. * Experience with workflow automation tools (Zapier, Make, or similar). * Exposure to travel booking workflows, GDS or OTA tools, or corporate travel management. To apply, please include * A brief summary of your experience managing multiple inboxes and multiple calendars for a single executive. * Examples of AI or automation tools you’ve used to manage email , calendar, or workflows (ChatGPT, Copilot, Zapier, etc.). * A short walkthrough of this scenario:?You log in at the start of your day and see 80+ new email s spread across three inboxes and multiple calendars with overlapping holds/requests. Describe step-by-step how you would triage the email s, clean up the calendars, and what you would surface to me in the first 30–60 minutes.

title: Bookkeeper to Financial Analyst (Full-Time, Long-Term, US Company)
job_title: Bookkeeper to Financial Analyst (Full-Time, Long-Term, US Company)
description: ## About OODA We are an AI-native short-term rental management company. We run over 100 properties with a small team and heavy automation, and we are deliberately the opposite of the legacy property managers our owners left behind. Most management companies treat the books as a back-office afterthought. We do not. Every owner gets a transparent monthly statement that ties every dollar to a specific property and a specific reservation. The person who owns that accuracy is one of the most trusted people in the company, and right now we are hiring that person. ## About the Role This role starts as our bookkeeper and is built to grow into our financial analyst. In the first phase, you own the daily books: categorizing hundreds of bank transactions a month, matching receipts and payouts to the correct property, reconciling reservation income, and producing clean owner invoices on time. Our financial system runs on ClickUp and Supabase with heavy automation, not a single off-the-shelf tool, so you will learn our way of doing things. As you master the books, the role grows. You move into financial analysis: contribution margin by property, profit-and-loss accuracy, cash-flow reconciliation, and the financial KPIs that tell us which properties and which decisions actually make money. The path is Bookkeeper, then Financial Analyst, then Controller. We are not hiring someone to only keep records. We are hiring someone who wants to understand the money and eventually help us run it. ## Who We're Looking For **You have real bookkeeping experience.** - You have reconciled accounts, categorized transactions, and matched receipts and payments before. Property management or hospitality experience is a plus, not a requirement. **You are accurate at volume.** - We process hundreds of transactions a month. You hold a 99%+ categorization standard, and you do not let things slip when the volume is high. **You are fluent with systems, and you like that we use AI.** - We run on ClickUp, Supabase, and internal AI agents, and we use Claude and automation aggressively. You learn new tools quickly and lean into that instead of resisting it. **You are an analyst in waiting.** - You are not satisfied with only recording numbers, you want to understand them. You know (or want to learn) what contribution margin is, what drives a property's profit, and why a number moved. You ask what a number means, not just where it goes. **You own your work and communicate clearly.** - Your written English is clear. You flag problems early instead of hiding them. You suggest process improvements because you would rather fix the system than repeat the same manual task. ## What "Great" Looks Like **First 30 days:** You have learned our ClickUp and Supabase financial system, you understand our property portfolio, and you reconcile and categorize transactions independently to our time standard. **First 90 days:** You consistently hit our reconciliation-timeliness and accuracy KPIs, owner statements go out on time, and you have surfaced at least three process improvements. **First 180 days:** You own the monthly close with minimal review, and you begin producing contribution-margin and profit-and-loss views per property. **First 365 days:** You function as our financial analyst. You own the financial KPI picture, you can tell us the contribution margin of any property, and you help Christian make pricing and cost decisions from the numbers. You are on the path to Controller. ## Compensation & Growth - **This is a base-plus-KPI role, and we want you to understand that up front.** Your pay is tied to your performance, not just to being present. - **Base pay: $6 to $10 per hour**, set by your qualifications and experience, with room to move up the range as you build tenure and prove results. - **KPI performance bonus: 30% of your base**, earned by hitting your accounting KPIs. The KPIs are concrete and you will always know them: reconciliation timeliness, categorization accuracy, on-time owner statements, and, as you grow, the quality and timeliness of your financial analysis. The better you perform against them, the more you earn. - **Growth is structured, not vague.** Bookkeeper, then Financial Analyst, then Controller. Your base moves up the range with experience and tenure, and your bonus rewards performance. - You report directly to the founder. ## Schedule & Commitment - **Full-time, 9:00am to 5:00pm, Monday to Friday, Philippines time.** - This is your one job. We expect your full attention during these hours. We do not accept candidates who are running other jobs, freelance clients, or side work during the workday. If you are looking for a part-time role to stack alongside two others, this is not the one. - We are remote and we trust you to work your hours, and that trust depends on you being present and focused during them. ## The Hard Parts (we are being honest) - High transaction volume that demands real attention to detail. - Firm turnaround standards. The books close on a schedule, not when it is convenient. - A custom system you have to learn. We will train you, but you have to want to learn it. - We measure performance. You are rewarded for results, not for logging hours. ## How to Apply To apply, reply with this exact sentence: **"I am looking for a full time job and understand that this is a 9-5 where I will not be able to have other clients."**

title: Ecommerce Fulfillment & Shipping Operations Coordinator
description: ABOUT THE ROLE We're a premium direct-to-consumer apparel brand selling mainly to US customers, with manufacturing in Asia and warehouses in the US. We're hiring a hands-on Fulfillment & Shipping Operations Coordinator to run the daily operations that get orders shipped correctly, keep our inventory accurate, and keep our shipping costs in check. YOUR THREE PRIORITIES (what you'll be measured on) 1. Inventory accuracy. Make sure we never lose stock; when stock is lost, file and recover the claim; and keep inventory counts accurate and matched across every system. 2. Getting orders to customers. Fast fulfillment from the ---------- nt an order is placed, fast delivery from the ---------- nt it ships, and quick resolution of any issue along the way. 3. Costs. Verify every shipping, warehouse, and returns charge is accurate, and continuously find ways to reduce those costs. HOW THE ROLE WORKS The core of this job is daily: making sure orders flow to the right warehouse, handling the exceptions our automation can't, and working our issue/tracking boards (shipping issues, unfulfilled orders, late deliveries) through to resolution every business day. Around that sits a lighter set of monthly tasks (inbound receiving, inventory checks, a few reports, and carrier-invoice verification) — much of which is already automated, so the job is to run and verify those, not build them by hand. You'll work across our ecommerce platform, order-management and warehouse systems, and a project/issue-tracking tool, coordinate with the team over chat, and follow written SOPs. Hours are standard Philippine business hours (about 9am–6pm PHT); no night shift. Working time is tracked with a time-tracking tool. This is NOT entry-level. You should have run ecommerce fulfillment before, be comfortable learning and working across multiple systems, stay organized under a daily queue, and communicate clearly and promptly. If you go quiet when things get hard, this isn't for you. If you take ownership and keep things moving without being chased, you'll do well here. WHAT YOU'LL DO Daily — order fulfillment (priority 2): - Oversee the daily order flow. Most orders route to the right warehouse automatically; you make sure the daily outbound completes cleanly and handle the exceptions. - Process manual-override cases: split orders across two warehouses, international orders (purchase/register the shipping label, attach the commercial invoice), and reshipments. - Reconcile edited/held orders between the store and the warehouse system. Daily — shipping-issue & delivery resolution (priority 2): - Own the issue boards end to end: log each issue, classify it, respond to the customer within 24 hours, follow up with the warehouse/carrier on a set cadence, resolve it (reship/refund/claim), and close it out. - Clear open/unfulfilled orders flagged by automation within SLA. - Track late or non-moving shipments and drive resolution with the warehouses and carriers. Inventory accuracy (priority 1): - Receive inbound shipments using documentation from Procurement; build the inbound records, reconcile against the packing list, and log any shortages/damage. - Run the monthly inventory checks (store-vs-warehouse, plus an internal check) and fix discrepancies so stock matches across systems. - When a warehouse loses or mishandles stock, file the claim and follow it through to recovery. - Produce the monthly inventory/inbound/outbound/delivery reports — run them, sanity-check the output, and fix anything that looks off. Costs (priority 3): - Verify freight, storage, and returns invoices against rate cards using our in-house tool; flag and recover overcharges. - Continuously look for ways to lower shipping and fulfillment costs (e.g., right-sizing packaging, improving routing, catching recurring billing errors). REQUIREMENTS - 3–5 years' hands-on ecommerce fulfillment / shipping / order operations (running the systems, not physical warehouse work). - Strong experience with a major ecommerce platform (multi-location orders and inventory). - Experience with order-management/ERP software and third-party warehouse (3PL) systems. - Experience running an issue/ticket board to a daily SLA. - Strong spreadsheet skills; comfortable with AI-assisted reporting (a plus). - Able to audit carrier invoices against rate cards and spot overcharges. - Excellent written English and fast, reliable communication. - High attention to detail; dependable during PH business hours; comfortable logging time via a time-tracker; self-manages from written SOPs. Nice to have: experience with returns and help-desk platforms; apparel/fashion ecommerce; US shipping & customs (DDP/DDU). HOW TO APPLY (please follow exactly — applications that skip these will not be reviewed) 1. Start your reply with the word XPRESS so I know you read the full post. 2. A short paragraph on your most relevant fulfillment/operations role: which platforms you used and what you personally owned. 3. Scenario A: An order shipped from our warehouse three days ago, but the tracking hasn't moved since. Walk me through how you'd resolve it — what you'd check, who you'd contact, and on what cadence. 4. Scenario B: An order has two items, and each needs to ship from a different warehouse. How would you handle splitting and processing it? 5. What ecommerce platform, order-management/warehouse systems, and issue-tracking tools have you used directly, and for how long? 6. How comfortable are you using AI tools to run or check reports? Give an example if you have one. 7. Your typical working hours in Philippine time, and the longest you've stayed in one fulfillment/operations role.

title: Growth Executive Assistant (Content + Marketing + Operations)
description: Build. Grow. Scale. I’m looking for someone to become my right hand. I own multiple successful businesses, but your primary mission is simple: Help grow Signum Scientific from approximately $10,000/month back to $20,000+/month—and far beyond. Signum Scientific operates within the research peptide industry, one of the fastest-growing and most highly regulated markets in e-commerce. Success in this industry requires creativity, discipline, and a strong understanding of compliance. This is not an influencer role, and it is not a typical social media job. Every piece of content must be created with compliance in mind. We cannot make medical claims, promise results, or market products in ways that violate platform policies or industry regulations. If you aren’t willing to learn the nuances of operating in a regulated industry, this probably isn’t the right fit. If that challenge excites you, keep reading. Your Primary Mission Your focus is helping Signum Scientific grow. That means creating consistent, high-quality content that builds trust, educates our audience, strengthens our brand, and ultimately drives sales. Once Signum reaches our growth targets and has strong systems in place, you’ll begin supporting my other companies, including Foamaha Parties, Main Street Carnival, Putt & ParTee, and Marquee Activations. Responsibilities Marketing & Content * Develop and manage a daily content calendar * Create short-form video content (Instagram Reels, TikTok, YouTube Shorts) * Design graphics and educational content * Write captions, email s, and marketing copy * Schedule and manage social media across multiple platforms * Repurpose content into multiple formats * Monitor analytics and identify opportunities for growth * Research trends while maintaining compliance with industry regulations * Help execute product launches and promotional campaigns Executive Assistant Responsibilities Help me stay focused on high-value work by handling operational tasks such as: * Calendar management * Inbox organization * Research * Project coordination * Follow-up reminders * SOP documentation * Travel planning * General executive support Who I’m Looking For You are: * Highly organized * Self-motivated * Creative * Fast * Detail-oriented * Comfortable using AI tools like ChatGPT * Able to work independently * Always looking for ways to improve systems and increase revenue Most importantly, you think like an owner—not just an employee. If you see an opportunity, you bring it forward. Experience Preferred * Canva * CapCut * ChatGPT * Meta Business Suite * Instagram * Facebook * TikTok * YouTube * Google Workspace * WordPress or WooCommerce (preferred) * Email marketing platforms Experience in healthcare, supplements, peptides, biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, or other regulated industries is a major plus—but not required if you’re eager to learn. Compensation I believe exceptional people deserve exceptional compensation. You’ll receive competitive base pay based on your experience. However, the largest earning opportunity will come through performance-based incentives tied directly to the growth of Signum Scientific. If your work helps drive meaningful revenue growth, I want you to share in that success. I’m looking for someone who wants to build something meaningful and be rewarded for producing real results—not just completing tasks. Success Looks Like Within your first 90 days: * Daily content is being published consistently. * Brand awareness and engagement are growing. * Marketing systems are organized and repeatable. * I’m spending significantly less time on administrative work. * Signum Scientific is on a clear trajectory back toward $20,000+ in monthly revenue. How to Apply Please include: * Your resume * Examples of social media accounts you’ve managed * Examples of content you’ve created (videos, graphics, campaigns, etc.) * A short introduction about yourself * A brief explanation of how you would help grow a premium brand operating in a regulated industry Bonus: Share one content idea or marketing campaign you believe could help grow Signum Scientific while remaining compliant with industry regulations. If you’re looking for a position where your ideas matter, your work has a direct impact on revenue, and your compensation can grow alongside the business, I’d love to hear from you.
